solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criminal reproduces rare carbon copy fakes

indicators.note: to reproduce here is to make the letters over again in a new order

parts.note: cc is the standard abbreviation for carbon copy on a letter or email

explanation.surface: A con artist turns out forged duplicates of something scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduces' looks like the criminal's copying, but it signals reshuffling RARE, CC and FAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who breaks open strongboxes to steal their contents is a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Barren as rainfall is deficient principally

indicators.note: principally points to the principal, leading letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Land is barren because there has been too little rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe land too dry to grow anything; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Interested in Old English? Only when transposed

indicators.note: transposed says the two pieces given in the clue swap places, so English comes before old

parts.note: old means aged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is keen on Anglo-Saxon, answering that only if the language is turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old English' reads as the early language, but it is two pieces; 'Only when transposed' tells you to put the English piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: To be engrossed or occupied with something is to have one's interest held by it, a synonym sense.

clue.text: Part of Chester area is excellent

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A district around the English city of Chester is praised as first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'is excellent' is narrowed to 'excellent': 'is' links wordplay to definition, and an adjective is needed to match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In older or informal British use, a rare time or rare treat is a splendid, first-class one.

clue.text: Fried bread's mis-shapen contour

indicators.note: something mis-shapen has its form twisted out of true, so the letters of the word are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of fried bread has come out with a lopsided outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of bread fried or toasted crisp, served in soup or salad.

clue.text: Frightening endings to Poe tale — horror story

indicators.note: endings to points to the final letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: The conclusions of Edgar Allan Poe's horror tales are scary.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of eerie, meaning uncanny and frightening; a synonym.

clue.text: Kind of tour undertaken by would-be MP gallivanting with less time to work

definitions.text: Kind of tour undertaken by would-be MP

indicators.note: gallivanting is gadding about, so the letters of the two words roam into a new order

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A parliamentary candidate tours about with too little time to get any work done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gallivanting' rearranges WITH LESS into WHISTLES; 'to' just joins time and work. An MP is a Member of the British Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign tour of many brief stops in small places, as made by election candidates.

clue.text: Fellow in German committee provides violin part

parts.note: a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A man sitting on a German committee supplies a piece of a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but simply supplies its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip of wood on a violin's neck against which the strings are pressed is a component of the instrument.

clue.text: This reactor is a speedy generator

parts.note: speedy means fast
a breeder is one who generates offspring

explanation.surface: A reactor is described as a rapid producer.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay also nods to the real meaning: such a reactor generates more fissile fuel than it uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor using fast neutrons that produces more fissile material than it consumes is a type of reactor.

clue.text: A red kestrel destroyed hat

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A red bird of prey has wrecked someone's headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth cap with peaks front and back and ear flaps, associated with Sherlock Holmes, is a kind of headwear.

clue.text: Silly bride and Brian start to dally inappropriately

indicators.note: inappropriately suggests things out of their proper place, so the letters of the two names are put in a new order
start to points to the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A wedding couple begin to flirt or dawdle when they should not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inappropriately' sits at the end and reshuffles all that comes before it, including the letter picked by 'start to'; 'and' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the brain of a bird, an informal insult meaning foolish or stupid.

clue.text: Druggie's endless cure finally succeeded

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for cure is cut off

parts.note: to cure is to heal

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word succeeded

explanation.surface: An addict's never-ending treatment at last works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter from HEAL, leaving HEA.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a head is a habitual drug user, as in pothead or acidhead.

clue.text: Mythical creature's still on island

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'yet to come'
I is an abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A legendary beast is still living on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of Himalayan legend is a creature of myth.

clue.text: Bag refurbished chalet after first of September

indicators.note: after says the rearranged chalet comes after that opening letter
first of points to the opening letter of the word September
refurbished means done up anew, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A holiday chalet gets done up at the start of September, as a school bag might.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder bag with a flap, traditionally carried by schoolchildren, is a type of bag.

clue.text: Flower rim mostly black in the centre

indicators.note: mostly says most of the word for rim is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a lip is the rim of a cup or jug

indicators.note: in the centre points to the middle letters of the word black, its ends left off

explanation.surface: A flower has a petal edge that is mainly dark in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rim' looks like part of the flower, but it is the edge of a cup; 'mostly' and 'in the centre' both trim letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub with fragrant purple or white blossom, so an example of a flower.

clue.text: Screened Conservative deliveries to journalist

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
ed, short for editor, is a crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A Tory politician hid documents being handed to a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled in succession, so 'deliveries' gives OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden or shielded from view; to screen something is to cover it.

clue.text: Tree nut hugs hollow Acer

indicators.note: hugs says the word for nut wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a cob is a hazelnut

indicators.note: hollow says the inside of the word Acer is emptied, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A nut is wedged inside the hollow trunk of a maple.
explanation.walkthrough: Acer is the botanical name for the maple, a tree in the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean locust bean tree, whose pods are used as a chocolate substitute.

clue.text: Whereon dead Russian tsar might have rested

definitions.text: Whereon dead Russian tsar might have rested

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
Ivan was the name of several tsars, notably Ivan the Terrible

explanation.surface: A late Russian emperor may have lain on a couch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of a couch on which a tsar could recline.
explanation.definitionFit: A low backless couch or sofa is a piece of furniture someone might lie on.

clue.text: Instrument involved in early recording

indicators.note: involved in says the answer is wrapped up inside the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: An instrument played on an early recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stringed harp of ancient Greece is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Prison disturbance

definitions.meaning: slang for jail, as in doing time in the nick
a commotion or fuss, as in causing a great fuss

explanation.surface: A riot in a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a slang word for a jail, and an uproar or commotion.

clue.text: Police district's reported method

indicators.note: reported says the word is heard rather than read, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a manner is a way or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A police area's procedure has been written up.
explanation.walkthrough: In British police slang a manor is the patch a station or officer covers.
explanation.definitionFit: London police slang for an area of jurisdiction, from the old landed estate sense.

clue.text: Corresponded then married in Switzerland. Quite the reverse!

indicators.note: in would put the word for married inside the code for Switzerland
Quite the reverse tells you to swap the roles, so the Swiss code goes inside the word for married

parts.note: mated means paired off or married
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A couple wrote to each other, then wed in Switzerland, or rather the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'in' would put the married word inside the Swiss code; 'Quite the reverse!' swaps container and contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that match agree or correspond with each other, a synonym.

clue.text: Met Tina on the third of April unexpectedly

indicators.note: the third of points to the third letter of the word April
unexpectedly says the letters turn up in a surprise order

explanation.surface: Bumped into Tina by chance on the third day of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the third of April' looks like a date but picks the third letter of 'April', which joins TINA and ON in the rearrangement signalled by 'unexpectedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone by chance is to meet them; the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Varnish outside framework with a touch of creosote

parts.note: a shell is the outer framework of a building

indicators.note: a touch of points to just the first letter of the word creosote

explanation.surface: Wood finish for an exterior structure, with a little creosote added.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin from the lac insect used to make a hard varnish, so a type of varnish.

clue.text: Germs could become biological without processed goo

indicators.note: could become says the letters of the next word could be reformed
without says the letters of goo are subtracted before the rest is rearranged

explanation.surface: Germs might turn biological if processed slime were absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Take G, O, O from BIOLOGICAL and rearrange what is left; 'processed' only says goo's letters needn't be in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod-shaped bacteria, often disease-causing, are microbes, popularly called germs.

clue.text: Fondness on a regular basis for poetry

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking every other letter of the word fondness

explanation.surface: Someone has a recurring liking for verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject, collectively a form of poetry.

clue.text: Second bit of dirt falls to bottom of storage tank

indicators.note: Second bit of points to the second letter of the word for dirt
falls to bottom says that letter drops to the end of the down entry

parts.note: soil is earth or dirt

explanation.surface: Dirt settles to the base of a storage container.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the bottom is the end, so the O of SOIL moves after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower or pit for storing grain, fodder or missiles, a kind of storage tank.

clue.text: I must leave outstanding cook

indicators.note: must leave says the letter I departs from the word for outstanding

parts.note: chief means principal or most outstanding

explanation.surface: A first-rate cook declares that the speaker has to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional cook, especially the head cook in a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Fine summer in Provence for holiday

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
ete is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: A lovely Provençal summer for a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: Provence is in France, so summer there is the French word été.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival or feast day, as in a saint's day, is a holiday; also a village fair.

clue.text: Handled soft fabric

definitions.meaning: touched with the hands, the past of to touch
a non-woven cloth of pressed wool used for hats

explanation.surface: Fingered some soft cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: touched with the hand, and a matted woollen cloth.

clue.text: Blow! Not a left-footer

definitions.meaning: a punch thrown with the stronger fist
someone who favours the side opposite the left, with a nod to left-footer as old slang for a Catholic

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance about someone who is not a left-footed player.
explanation.walkthrough: Left-footer is British slang for a Roman Catholic, so the second reading teasingly suggests a Protestant too.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a punch from the dominant fist, and a person who favours their right side.

clue.text: Promise by speaker is verbal

parts.note: to give one's word is to promise
of can mean by, as in a play of Shakespeare
the mouth is the organ that speaks

explanation.surface: A spoken pledge from someone talking is oral rather than written.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed on by speech rather than writing, so spoken or oral, used adjectivally.
